findings.impact: Every file question's citations event (text path rag.py:695, 862, 982 and the frames path) now runs through new code. As read, the result is the same: a number is kept when it is in 1..len(chunks), and the position is the chunk's position. No user-visible change was found.
findings.evidence: addons/intelligence/app/rag/file_question.py:1012-1041: citations() builds {index: chunk.position} and calls citations_from, which tests `number not in positions` where the old code tested `1 <= number <= len(chunks)`. Callers outside the touch points are at rag.py:695, rag.py:862 and rag.py:982.
findings.repro: not_reproduced; equivalence was reasoned from the code.

bucket_proposal.reason: An unplanned reach outside the declared touch points; it is behaviour-equivalent and breaks no invariant.

findings.claim: rag.py now defines _call_times twice, and the later definition silently replaces the first, so the first is dead code outside the planned edits.
findings.impact: No runtime effect. A reader who edits the first definition (rag.py:1593) changes nothing, which could lead to a wrong fix of frame-call parsing.

findings.repro: Read the module: _tool_plan at rag.py:1681 resolves _call_times to the second definition.

bucket_proposal.reason: Reads wrong and was not planned; it breaks no invariant.

findings.claim: The fit check reserves the longest stop note but not the newline that joins it to the result, so a stop result can be 3,001 characters when its clock time has 8 characters (a row starting at 10 h or later).
findings.impact: On a video of 10 hours or more, a transcript result that stops at a row whose start is at or after 10:00:00, with the earlier text exactly at the boundary, is one character over the 3,000-character cap. This is practically unreachable in normal use.
findings.evidence: rag.py:1912-1914: an accepted row satisfies len(join(lines+group)) + _TRANSCRIPT_STOP_CHARS <= 3000, where _TRANSCRIPT_STOP_CHARS uses an 8-character time (rag.py:733). On stop the result is join(lines) + '\n' + stop note (rag.py:1914, 1930). With format_position giving 'HH:MM:SS' (8 characters) at 10 h or later (prompt.py:266-273), the total is the accepted length + 1 + _TRANSCRIPT_STOP_CHARS, which can be 3,001. For 7-character clocks or shorter, the slack absorbs the newline.
findings.repro: not_reproduced. Construct rows starting at 36000 s so that the previous accepted candidate is exactly 3000 - _TRANSCRIPT_STOP_CHARS characters long, then request a range whose next row does not fit; len(result) == 3001.

bucket_proposal.reason: I3 bounds the result, stop note included, at 3,000 characters.

findings.proposed_fix: Reserve _TRANSCRIPT_STOP_CHARS + 1 (the joining newline) in the fit check.

findings.claim: An unexpected exception while a transcript result is built is not routed to the fallback; _serve_transcript runs outside any try in the serving loop.
findings.impact: No ordinary trigger was found (the function is pure over in-memory rows). If one existed, the stream would end abnormally instead of sending today's request.
findings.evidence: rag.py:1410-1427 calls _serve_transcript after the cut_task try block has closed; only the outer try/finally (rag.py:1229/1502) surrounds it, and that block only logs.

bucket_proposal.reason: Spec section 3 sends such an error to fallback, but no declared invariant covers it, and there is no ordinary trigger.

findings.claim: No test kills dropping the `sent_as == "filtered"` condition: a first-segment row that an earlier call already sent with its stored text would get a supplement again, and the tests do not notice.
findings.impact: A regression that re-sends removed parts under a new number for a row already sent with stored text would pass the suite.
findings.evidence: rag.py:1900. In test_a_later_call_does_not_send_the_removed_parts_again, the only removed part (HEADER) is already in sent_parts from the first call's [12] supplement, so the mutant's supplement for [13]/[14] is empty and the asserted lines are unchanged.
findings.repro: Mental mutation: replace `if first and sent_as == "filtered":` with `if first:`. In the test above the second call still yields exactly the four 'already sent' lines and no HEADER, so the mutant survives.

bucket_proposal.reason: A test gap, not a code defect.

potential_unspecified_behavior.behavior: A single row longer than about 2,930 characters can never be sent; every transcript call whose range includes it returns only the stop note, and rows after it in time order are unreachable unless the range starts after that row ends.
potential_unspecified_behavior.reason: Triggered only by an unusually long transcript window; the model then sees 'Text from X on was not sent' on every attempt and answers without that part.

potential_unspecified_behavior.behavior: Removed parts already sent are tracked by their stripped text across all rows, not per row, so a sent first-segment row whose removed line was given in another row's supplement gets no supplement of its own.
potential_unspecified_behavior.reason: Several first-segment rows share a heading line; the model still received that line once, so the answer is unaffected.

potential_unspecified_behavior.behavior: Lines written as part of a first-segment row's stored text are not recorded in sent_parts, so a later supplement for another row can repeat a line the model already received in stored text.
potential_unspecified_behavior.reason: Repeated slide headings appear twice in the tool result, costing a few characters of the 3,000.

potential_unspecified_behavior.behavior: Cut material with no row that has a span (partial true but rows empty) is not offered get_transcript and keeps the uncut prompt and texts.
potential_unspecified_behavior.reason: A video whose text has no timed rows is not an ordinary case; the user would see no difference from today.
